# Documentation of removals pipeline and join to arrests/detention stays.

Goal: characterize interior deportations without double-counting.

Questions:

* What about records that have arrest, no detain, but have removal?
* What about removals more than 10 days after detention release?
* How to deal with/report logically-inconsistent records?

```{r setup}
options(scipen = 999)

library(tidyverse)

# arrests <- arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data/arrests-latest.parquet"))
# stints <- arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data/detention-stints-latest.parquet"))
stays <- arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data/detention-stays-latest.parquet"))
removals <- arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data/removals-latest.parquet"))
joined <- arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data/joined-arrests-detention-stays-latest.parquet"))
joined_w_removals <- arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data/joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals-diff.parquet")) # Interim file with diagnostic cols from join

```

```{r setup_data}

# Fixing one bad value that obscures real variation
# stays$departed_date[stays$departed_date == as.Date("1923-09-14")] <- as.Date("2023-09-14")

stays <- stays |>
  group_by(unique_identifier) |>
  mutate(n_departed_date = n_distinct(departed_date),
         n_stays = n_distinct(stay_ID)
         ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(bookout_to_deport_days = difftime(departed_date, stay_book_out_date_time, units = "days"),
         id_in_removals = unique_identifier %in% removals$unique_identifier)

# Fixing one bad value that obscures real variation
# joined$departed_date[joined$departed_date == as.Date("1923-09-14")] <- as.Date("2023-09-14")

joined <- joined |>
  group_by(unique_identifier) |>
  mutate(n_departed_date = n_distinct(departed_date),
         n_stays = n_distinct(stay_ID)
         ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(bookout_to_deport_days = difftime(departed_date, stay_book_out_date_time, units = "days"),
         id_in_removals = unique_identifier %in% removals$unique_identifier,
         arrest_wo_detention = is.na(stay_ID))

# (Bad value is not matched here)

joined_w_removals <- joined_w_removals |>
  group_by(unique_identifier) |>
  mutate(n_departed_date = n_distinct(departed_date_removal), # different field name here for now
         n_stays = n_distinct(stay_ID)
         ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(bookout_to_deport_days = difftime(departed_date_removal, stay_book_out_date_time, units = "days"), # different field name here for now
         id_in_removals = unique_identifier %in% removals$unique_identifier,
         arrest_wo_detention = is.na(stay_ID))

```

## What is structure of removals data currently in stays dataset (derived from detention stints)?

ICE detention data contain removal information (`departed_date`, `departure_country`) which are joined on an indeterminate key that is not included with released data (possibly "Subject ID"). In most cases, if an individual has multiple detention stays, and one ends with removal, stays preceding that removal inherit data from its removal field in what we can call a removal "episode" (set of stays preceding a removal). If an individual has no associated removal, removals fields are missing.

```{r stay_example_n_greater_than_1}

stays |> filter(n_stays > 1) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier) |>
  select(unique_identifier, stay_book_in_date_time, stay_book_out_date_time, stay_release_reason, departed_date) |>
  head(10)

```

Some individuals may have multiple removal episodes which follow the same logic:

```{r stay_example_n_greater_than_2}

stays |> filter(n_stays > 2) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier) |>
  select(unique_identifier, stay_book_in_date_time, stay_book_out_date_time, stay_release_reason, departed_date) |>
  head(10)

```

In the majority of cases, the presence of removal information is logically consistent with this table structure, e.g. absent for those never removed across available data; or present for those removed according to available data. (Due to the removal episode logic described above, many stays that do not end in removal have removal information associated with another stay or removal episode, this is expected, but could lead to double-counting of removals if not accounted for.)

However, a small number of records have removal information for which the source is unclear (removal information in the detentions table but no associated records in the removals dataset) or missing (stay is categorized as a removal but neither detentions nor removals have associated information).

```{r}

stays <- stays |>
  mutate(is_removal = stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"),
        departed_date_from_detentions = !is.na(departed_date),
        interpretation = case_when(
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Never removed",
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal associated with different episode",
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Removal info source unclear",
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal associated with later stay in episode",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Removal info missing",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal info available but not associated with stay",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Removal info source unclear",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal info present"
        ))

stays |> count(is_removal, departed_date_from_detentions, id_in_removals, interpretation) |>
  mutate(pct = (n / sum(n)) * 100)

```

Aside: Arrests without detentions in joined table mostly don't have associated removal info; for those that do most removals are likely linked to a different arrest/detention episode. (How would we test this?)

```{r}

joined <- joined |>
  mutate(is_removal = stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"),
        departed_date_from_detentions = !is.na(departed_date),
        interpretation = case_when(
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Never removed",
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal associated with different episode",
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Removal info source unclear",
          is_removal == FALSE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal associated with later stay in episode",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Removal info missing",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == FALSE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal info available but not associated with stay",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == FALSE ~ "Removal info source unclear",
          is_removal == TRUE & departed_date_from_detentions == TRUE & id_in_removals == TRUE ~ "Removal info present"
        ))

joined |> 
  filter(arrest_wo_detention) |>
  count(is_removal, departed_date_from_detentions, id_in_removals, interpretation) |>
  mutate(pct = (n / sum(n)) * 100)

```

 `departed_date` in stays includes a small number of values outside of scope of removals dataset:

```{r}

dat <- stays |>
  dplyr::select(departed_date, departure_country) |>
  mutate(dataset = "stays") |>
  rbind(removals |>
    dplyr::select(departed_date, departure_country) |>
    mutate(dataset="removals"))

dat |> group_by(dataset) |>
  summarize(min_departed_date = min(departed_date, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_departed_date = max(departed_date, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_before_fy23 = sum(departed_date < "2022-10-01", na.rm=TRUE),
            n_departure_country = length(unique(departure_country)))

```

## Comparison of removals data across datasets

In `joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals.R`, we follow the same steps used to join arrests with detention stays to join in removals which match to unique ID, and fall within five days before and ten days after detention book out.

Removals this will fail to match:

* Removals outside -5/+10 days of detention book out
* Removals not associated with detention
* Removals outside the timeframe of removals data (2022-10-01 to 2026-08-09)

Questions:

* Do we want to pass `departed_date` and other removals info from detentions through if it fails to merge in from removals table? If so, what criteria?
* How should we deal with matches to stays that don't end in removal?

```{r}

cols_to_select <- c("stay_ID", "stay_book_in_date_time", "stay_book_out_date_time", "departed_date", "bookout_to_deport_days", "departure_country", "stay_release_reason", "n_departed_date", "n_stays", "id_in_removals")

removals_via_stays <- stays |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return")) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier) |>
  select(all_of(cols_to_select)) |>
  mutate(dataset = "stays")

removals_via_joined <- joined |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return")) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier) |>
  select(all_of(cols_to_select)) |>
  mutate(dataset = "joined-arrests-detention-stays")

removals_via_joined_w_removals <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return")) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier) |>
  select(all_of(cols_to_select)) |>
  mutate(dataset = "joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals")

dat <- rbind(removals_via_stays, removals_via_joined) |>
  rbind(removals_via_joined_w_removals) |>
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset,
         levels = c("stays",
                    "joined-arrests-detention-stays",
                    "joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals"),
         ordered = TRUE))

```

Here we compare summary stats for stays ending in removal in three datasets: "stays", "joined-arrests-detention-stays", and "joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals". This is not super informative but we note that "joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals" retains all records in "joined-arrests-detention-stays" and bookout date to deportation date range matches criteria above. Slightly lower proportion of records correspond to IDs in removals--why? Negative average detention bookout to deportation date is because detention stay bookout is datetime variable and departure is just date. Most departed date are same day as detention book out.

```{r}

tab1 <- dat |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean_bookout_to_deport_days = as.numeric(mean(bookout_to_deport_days, na.rm=TRUE)),
            med_bookout_to_deport_days = as.numeric(median(bookout_to_deport_days, na.rm=TRUE)),
            min_bookout_to_deport_days = as.numeric(min(bookout_to_deport_days, na.rm=TRUE)),
            max_bookout_to_deport_days = as.numeric(max(bookout_to_deport_days, na.rm=TRUE)),
            mean_n_stays = mean(n_stays, na.rm=TRUE),
            med_n_stays = median(n_stays, na.rm=TRUE),
            mean_n_departed_date = mean(n_departed_date, na.rm=TRUE),
            med_n_departed_date = median(n_departed_date, na.rm=TRUE),
            n_ids_not_in_removals = sum(id_in_removals == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE),
            pct_ids_in_removals = (sum(id_in_removals, na.rm=TRUE) / n()) * 100,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  # # Format each type, then everything is character and can share one column
  # mutate(
  #   across(where(\(x) inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXt"))),
  #          \(x) format(x, "%Y-%m-%d")),
  #   across(where(is.integer),
  #          \(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
  #   across(where(is.double),
  #          \(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","))
  # ) |>
  pivot_longer(-dataset, names_to = "stat", values_to = "value") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = value)

tab1
```

Table exported from `joined-arrests-detention-stays-removals.R` includes removals fields derived from both detentions and removals tables, so we can compare values pre- and post-merge.

```{r}

diff_dat <- joined_w_removals %>%
  mutate(is_removal = stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"),
        departed_date_from_detentions = !is.na(departed_date),
          match = !is.na(removal_ID),
         diff_departed_date = if_else(
          condition = departed_date != departed_date_removal,
          true = TRUE,
          false = FALSE,
          missing = NA),
        new_date = is.na(departed_date) & !is.na(departed_date_removal),
        lost_date = !is.na(departed_date) & is.na(departed_date_removal),
        is_same_departure_country = departure_country == departure_country_removal,
        id_in_removals = unique_identifier %in% removals$unique_identifier,
        bookout_to_deport_days = difftime(departed_date, as.Date(stay_book_out_date_time), units = "days"),
        bookout_to_deport_days_removal = difftime(departed_date_removal, as.Date(stay_book_out_date_time), units = "days")
        ) |>
  select(unique_identifier,
         stay_ID,
         removal_ID,
         stay_book_out_date_time,
         stay_release_reason,
         departed_date,
         departed_date_removal,
         bookout_to_deport_days,
         bookout_to_deport_days_removal,
         diff_departed_date,
         new_date,
         lost_date,
         is_same_departure_country,
         id_in_removals,
         is_removal,
         departed_date_from_detentions,
         match) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

lookup <- tribble(
  ~is_removal, ~match, ~id_in_removals, ~departed_date_from_detentions, ~diff_departed_date, ~interpretation, ~status,
  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, "Match, agrees with detentions table", "OK",
  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  "Match, disagrees with detentions table", "investigate",
  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, NA,    "Match, no departed date in detentions table", "OK",
  TRUE,  FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE,  NA,    "No match, departed date in detentions table and ID present in removals", "pass through?",
  TRUE,  FALSE, TRUE,  FALSE, NA,    "No match, no departed date in detentions table but ID present in removals", "investigate",
  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,  NA,    "No match, ID not present in removals but departed date in detentions table", "pass through?",
  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, NA,    "No match, no removals data", "BAD (missing data?)",
  FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, "Stay doesn't end in removal, but we match same date as present in detentions table", "OK (We're not explicitly excluding non-removals from match)",
  FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  "Stay doesn't end in removal, we match different date than detentions table", "investigate",
  FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, NA,    "Stay doesn't end in removal, we match, no date in detentions table", "investigate",
  FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE,  NA,    "Stay doesn't end in removal, we don't match, but ID in removals and departed date in detentions table", "OK (Probably removed on another stay)",
  FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,  FALSE, NA,    "Stay doesn't end in removal, but ID in removals table", "OK (Probably removed on another stay)",
  FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,  NA,    "Stay doesn't end in removal, departed date in detentions but no ID in removals table", "BAD (missing data?)",
  FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, NA,    "Stay doesn't end in removal, no removals data", "OK (Never/not yet removed)"
)

diff_dat <- diff_dat |>
   left_join(lookup, by = c("is_removal", "match", "id_in_removals", "departed_date_from_detentions", "diff_departed_date"))

stopifnot(sum(is.na(diff_dat$interpretation)) == 0)

```

We match some records that aren't removals because we don't try to exclude those explicitly

```{r}

tab4 <- diff_dat |>
   count(interpretation, status) |>
   mutate(pct = (n / sum(n) * 100)) |>
   arrange(desc(n))

knitr::kable(tab4)
```

## Assemble and test in tiers

### Tier 1: Match, agrees with detentions table 

Trivial matches for which departed dates in detentions and removals tables agree, departure clearly associated with stay that is correctly marked as removal.

```{r}

joined_w_removals <- joined_w_removals |>
  mutate(row_joined = row_number(),
         bookout_to_deport_days = difftime(departed_date, stay_book_out_date_time, units = "days"),
         bookout_to_deport_days_removal = difftime(departed_date_removal, stay_book_out_date_time, units = "days"), # different field name here for now
         )

t1 <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"), # is removal
         !is.na(removal_ID), # positive match
         !is.na(departed_date), # removal info via detentions table
         departed_date == departed_date_removal # removal info agrees
         ) |>
  mutate(tier = "T1: Good match",
         rule = "Join all desired removals fields")

stopifnot(sum(is.na(t1$unique_identifier)) == 0) # No missing unique IDs
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(t1$stay_ID)) == 0) # No duplicated stay IDs
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(t1$removal_ID)) == 0) # No duplicated removal IDs

joined_clean <- t1 |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

joined_remainder <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(!row_joined %in% joined_clean$row_joined)

stopifnot(nrow(joined_clean) + nrow(joined_remainder) == nrow(joined_w_removals))

```

### Tier 2: Stay doesn't end in removal, no removals data 

Trivial non-matches with no indication of removal, no overlap of unique IDs with tier 1. Almost 90% of stays accounted for in T1 + T2.

```{r}

t2 <- joined_remainder |>
  filter(!stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"), # is not removal
         is.na(removal_ID), # negative match
         !joined_remainder$unique_identifier %in% removals$unique_identifier, # not present in removals table
         is.na(departed_date), # no removal info via detentions table
         is.na(departed_date == departed_date_removal)  # removal info comparison null
         ) |>
  mutate(tier = "T2: Not removal, no removal info",
         rule = "Un-matched")

stopifnot(sum(is.na(t2$unique_identifier)) == 0) # No missing unique IDs
stopifnot(sum(t2$unique_identifier %in% t1$unique_identifier, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) # No overlap with T1
sum(is.na(t2$stay_ID)) / nrow(t2) # Proportion arrests without detentions

joined_clean <- rbind(joined_clean, t2) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

print(nrow(joined_clean) / nrow(joined_w_removals) * 100)

joined_remainder <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(!row_joined %in% joined_clean$row_joined)

stopifnot(nrow(joined_clean) + nrow(joined_remainder) == nrow(joined_w_removals))

```

### Tier 3: Remainder of trivially unmatchable records
 
 These are all flagged as removals because all non-removal records with these characteristics are in T2. Lack any removals data but look like plausible removals, e.g. last detention placement was at a staging facility.

```{r}

t3 <- joined_remainder |>
    filter(is.na(departed_date),
           !joined_remainder$unique_identifier %in% removals$unique_identifier, # not present in removals table
           !is.na(unique_identifier)
         ) |>
    mutate(tier = "T3: Non-matched removal, missing info",
           rule = "Un-matched, infer removal from detention bookout?")

t3 |>
  count(stay_release_reason) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

stopifnot(sum(t3$unique_identifier %in% t1$unique_identifier, na.rm=TRUE) == 0) # No overlap with T1 because no other associated removal
sum(t3$unique_identifier %in% t2$unique_identifier, na.rm=TRUE) / nrow(t3) # Minimal overlap with T2, indicating other stays that also don't have removal info

joined_clean <- rbind(joined_clean, t3) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

joined_remainder <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(!row_joined %in% joined_clean$row_joined)

stopifnot(nrow(joined_clean) + nrow(joined_remainder) == nrow(joined_w_removals))

```

### Tier 4: Arrests missing unique ID

Remaining non-removals missing unique ID (and therefore unmatchable to stays, removals, or other tiers). Keep departed date info where available but fail to match other removals data? How can we be sure not double counting with other records that do have unique ID?

```{r}

t4 <- joined_remainder |>
  filter(is.na(unique_identifier)) |>
  mutate(tier = "T4: Arrests missing unique ID",
         rule = "Un-matched, keep arrest departed date?")

t4 |>
  mutate(has_departed_date = !is.na(departed_date)) |>
  count(has_departed_date)

joined_clean <- rbind(joined_clean, t4) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

joined_remainder <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(!row_joined %in% joined_clean$row_joined)

stopifnot(nrow(joined_clean) + nrow(joined_remainder) == nrow(joined_w_removals))

```

Of remainder, 66K are not removal stays--could just say we don't care about any associated removals data, but would be nice to prove we captured it elsewhere

Of remainder, 30K are unique IDs with a match in T1

Of remainder, only 6520 are flagged as removals

### Tier 5: Matched removals lacking departed date via detentions table

Stays flagged as removals in detentions table but lacking departed date. We get new dates via match. Some of these are associated with other records in T1, should investigate. Check would be that multiple stays ending in removal don't overlap in some way?

```{r}

t5 <- joined_remainder |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"),
         is.na(departed_date),
         !is.na(removal_ID)) |>
  mutate(tier = "T5: Matched removals lacking departed date via detentions table",
         rule = "Keep new removal info")
         
t5 |>
  mutate(in_t1 = unique_identifier %in% t1$unique_identifier) |>
  count(in_t1)

joined_clean <- rbind(joined_clean, t5) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

joined_remainder <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(!row_joined %in% joined_clean$row_joined)

stopifnot(nrow(joined_clean) + nrow(joined_remainder) == nrow(joined_w_removals))

```

### T6: Removals that disagree with match

In >90% of cases we select a removal that is closer to detention book out time, but some exception where removals table carries a different date within match bounds.

```{r}

t6 <- joined_remainder |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"),
         !is.na(removal_ID)) |>
  mutate(tier = "T6: Matched removals which differ from departed date via detentions table",
         rule = "Keep new removal info")

t6 |>
  mutate(in_t1 = unique_identifier %in% t1$unique_identifier,
         closer_match = abs(bookout_to_deport_days_removal) < abs(bookout_to_deport_days)) |>
  dplyr::select(unique_identifier, stay_book_out_date_time, departed_date, departed_date_removal, bookout_to_deport_days, bookout_to_deport_days_removal, closer_match, in_t1) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

t6 |>
  summarize(sum(abs(bookout_to_deport_days_removal) < abs(bookout_to_deport_days))/ n())

joined_clean <- rbind(joined_clean, t6) |>
  arrange(unique_identifier)

joined_remainder <- joined_w_removals |>
  filter(!row_joined %in% joined_clean$row_joined)

stopifnot(nrow(joined_clean) + nrow(joined_remainder) == nrow(joined_w_removals))

```

### T7: Remaining unmatched removals

Why not matched? Presumably either out of bounds or associated removal not present in removals table.

```{r}

t7 <- joined_remainder |>
  filter(stay_release_reason %in% c("Removed", "Voluntary departure", "Voluntary Return", "Title 42 Return"),
         is.na(removal_ID)) |>
  mutate(tier = "T7: Remaining removals",
         rule = "")

t7 |> count(is.na(departed_date), id_in_removals)

```
